title: Garry Tan: Own your intelligence with personal AGI, a markdown brain and skill files
summary: Garry argues AGI is arriving diffused as a personal agent running on your own context, not as a single event. He lays out the stack (rented model + owned context + harness), a five-step plan to build a library and skill files, and argues skill files must be owned by you, not your employer.

principles.text: Personal AGI = frontier model (rented) + your context (owned) + a harness; the leverage is in context, not weights.
principles.quote: a frontier model which is rented and a commodity and getting cheaper by the quarter plus your context which is owned by you and unique

principles.text: Treat AI as a workforce, not autocomplete; same model yields 2x or 100x depending on context and timing.
principles.quote: the fastest growing founders we fund are not treating AI as autocomplete. They are treating it as a workforce.

principles.text: Start a brain as one folder of markdown files and compound daily; don't build the warehouse first.
principles.quote: Nobody builds the warehouse first. First, you build one shelf.

principles.text: Fat skills, thin harness: a skill is a page of English a smart intern could follow; markdown is code.
principles.quote: If a smart intern could follow it, an agent can run it.

principles.text: Split work between latent space (judgment, taste) and deterministic code (SQL, arithmetic, scripts).
principles.quote: The fix is having the model compute the way humans compute. the latent and the deterministic markdown files calling databases and scripts.

principles.text: Never do one-off work: skillify every task so learning compounds and you never ask twice.
principles.quote: If you have to ask for something twice, you failed.
